biodiversity_overview.text: 114,525 GBIF occurrence records for 86 tracked species are attributed to Madhya Pradesh, spanning 1870-2026.
111,941 of these records (97.7%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 31, Magnoliopsida 17, Mammalia 16, Squamata 8, Testudines 7, Amphibia 3, Actinopterygii 3, Crocodylia 1.

threatened_species.text: 10 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
4 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Tiger (EN), Mugger Crocodile (VU), Sloth Bear (VU), Asian Elephant (EN).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Cuckoo-shrike (15,628), Indian Grey-Hornbill (10,594), Indian Roller (9,106), Indian Griffon (7,587), Indian Cuckoo (5,702).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 1,540 in 2016 to 1,515 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 3.45% of Madhya Pradesh's area (48 areas intersect the state).
50.4% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (56,387 of 111,941); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Star Tortoise (0.61), Narrow-headed Softshell Turtle (0.54), Indian Softshell Turtle (0.49), Indian Spotted Creeper (0.49), Small Indian Mongoose (0.47).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Madhya Pradesh (equal-weight reference): cell near 22.875N 79.875E (overall rank 56, median rank across weightings 75); cell near 23.625N 77.625E (overall rank 71, median rank across weightings 103); cell near 22.875N 77.625E (overall rank 122, median rank across weightings 128).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 11,001 km2 (3.58% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

93.1 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (0.85% of the 2000 extent; 0.18% in 2015-2024, rank 24 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2006 (8.42 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 0.76% of land and population density is 275.1 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
38% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
